claim: Why not one democratic state for everyone?

heard.who: Edward Said, Palestinian scholar, in an Atlantic interview (1999)
heard.quote: One person, one vote, and let's have a truth and reconciliation commission.

heard.who: Peter Beinart, writer, in Jewish Currents (2020)
heard.quote: It is time for liberal Zionists to abandon the goal of Jewish-Palestinian separation and embrace the goal of Jewish-Palestinian equality.

answer: One state with equal votes would put Jews and Arabs at or near parity. Israel counts 7.79 million Jews and 'others' and 2.16 million Arabs; the Palestinian bureau counts 5.56 million in the West Bank and Gaza, East Jerusalem's Arabs in both. Yoram Ettinger of the American-Israel Demographic Research Group calls the Palestinian count inflated; DellaPergola and Soffer reject that. In DellaPergola's long-run 2024 projection, adding the West Bank to Israel leaves Jews about 60 percent, and adding Gaza just above 50. Israeli parties such as Yashar! oppose moves that would endanger the Jewish majority; one-state advocates such as Said and Beinart ask for equal votes. Our reading: one state with equal votes risks a Jewish majority, annexation without votes denies equal rights, and two states on the 1967 lines would keep both at the price of a border; the numbers explain the choice, they do not make it.

facts.text: Inside Israel's own count, the Central Bureau of Statistics reported on the eve of Independence Day 2026 a population of 10.244 million: 7.790 million Jews and 'others' (76 percent), 2.157 million Arabs (21.1 percent) and about 296,000 foreigners. 'Others' are mainly immigrants under the Law of Return who are not Jews in the population register; Arabs include Muslims, Arab Christians and Druze. The Ynet page reports this same release and DellaPergola's projection is built on CBS data, so the three citations are one dataset.

facts.text: The Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics (PCBS) itself reports, in its 31 December 2025 release, that the population of the State of Palestine reached about 5.56 million at the end of 2025, with 3.43 million in the West Bank and Gaza at about 2.1 million after a 10.6 percent fall in two years. Every Palestinian figure on this card traces to the PCBS: WAFA, the UN's West Bank figure (3,256,942 in 2023, cited from the PCBS beside 478,600 settlers from Israel's bureau) and the UN's Gaza figure (whose page names no source, so presumably the same data) are not independent counts; the Jerusalem Post's 2015 report is of an earlier PCBS release.

facts.text: The two bureaus overlap: Israel counts the roughly 300,000 Arab residents of East Jerusalem in its own census, and the Palestinian bureau counts them in the West Bank, so adding the two totals double-counts them; this rests on Kobi Michael of the Institute for National Security Studies, who told the Jerusalem Post in 2015 that it seemed the Palestinian bureau's report had double-counted them. DellaPergola's own 2005 estimates, published on an advocacy site beside the American Research Initiative's, state that East Jerusalem residents are not double counted in them.

facts.text: The Palestinian figures are disputed. In 2005-06 a study by the American Research Initiative, presented by the Jerusalem Center for Public Affairs, said the Palestinian Authority's population was 2.4 million, not the 3.8 million the PCBS reported; Yoram Ettinger, a member of the American-Israel Demographic Research Group, said in 2015 that the PCBS overstated the West Bank by 1.1 million. Demographers Sergio DellaPergola and Arnon Soffer rejected this: DellaPergola wrote in 2007 that the American Research Initiative's case rests on 'several assumptions, including that of a hugely exaggerated Palestinian base population', and Soffer accused Ettinger of drawing conclusions to serve a right-wing agenda. Ettinger's latest publication on the card, a May 2022 opinion piece in JNS, says the PCBS census includes 500,000 overseas residents who have been away over a year, in breach of international rules, and excludes 370,000 emigrants who left Judea and Samaria, and that there is annual net emigration shown by crossing records.

facts.text: Annexation of the West Bank without full citizenship, in its proponents' words: Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich proposed in September 2025 applying Israeli sovereignty to 82 percent of the West Bank, 'maximum land, minimum Arabs', keeping 'a clear Jewish majority' while Palestinians continue to govern themselves through the Palestinian Authority; he told Reuters he has 'no interest in letting them enjoy what the state of Israel has to offer'; MK Moshe Passal, in a response to Naftali Bennett carried by Israel National News (the page gives no date), proposed that Arab residents of Judea and Samaria 'should vote for the Jordanian parliament'. Defense Minister Israel Katz and, according to the Yesha Council as reported by Israel National News, most Likud ministers back sovereignty over most of Judea and Samaria; Religious Zionism's answer to Ynet is full sovereignty and 'hundreds of thousands of additional settlers'; Otzma Yehudit's is full sovereignty and 'voluntary migration' of Palestinians; and on 22 October 2025 the Knesset gave a sovereignty bill a preliminary 25 to 24 vote. We did not find the coalition agreements or party platforms themselves.

facts.text: The standard two-state version is two states on the 1967 lines with mutually agreed swaps: President Obama said so in 2011, the 2000 Clinton Parameters proposed a Palestinian state in 94 to 96 percent of the West Bank with swaps, and the September 2025 UN declaration endorsed 142 to 10 calls for a sovereign, viable Palestinian state.

DellaPergola: adding the West Bank keeps a Jewish majority but 'would render the idea of a Jewish and democratic state uncertain'. Critics such as the Joint List call that institutionalised apartheid, and Beinart argues that Israeli Jews' revealed preference is already one state in which millions lack basic rights.

Ettinger's own latest piece argues that overseas residents are included and emigrants excluded; DellaPergola's 2005 estimates, which accepted most of the PCBS count, put Jews at 51 percent of the population (54 percent with non-Jewish members of Jewish households).

could_not_verify: The Palestinian bureau's own release: pcbs.gov.ps would not load for our fetcher, so the 5.56 million figure rests on the Palestinian news agency WAFA reporting it, and UN figures only for Gaza (2.1 million) and, through a UN report, for the West Bank in 2023. We did not find the UN Population Division's own table.

A current independent audit of the Palestinian count: DellaPergola's 2024 study uses his own Palestinian projection; a peer-reviewed audit of the PCBS census was mentioned in a search summary but not read.
The American-Israel Demographic Research Group's current (2024-26) estimate: we found its 2005-06 and 2015 claims only.
Soffer's own words: read only through the Georgetown Berkley Center and the Jerusalem Post. DellaPergola's 2013 AP figures (6.9 million Jews, 6.5 million Arabs) are on an undated page.

Parties' platforms: Likud declined to answer the Ynet questionnaire and its platform was not read; Fatah's own platform and Edward Said's New York Times article were not read (we cite his Atlantic interview); Smotrich's 2017 Decisive Plan text could not be reached, so we quote his 2025 statements; Hamas's text is on the earlier card.
Whether the Palestinian Authority or Fatah supports 1967 lines with swaps in its own words: the UN page quoting Abbas does not say so; we have no read Palestinian primary document on that.

Fewer than three reliable sources: the CBS fact has two plus a government source; the Palestinian count has two plus a Palestinian government source; the double-counting fact; the confederation fact (one news, one opinion, one advocacy); the one-state and annexation facts rest on interviews and opinion pieces by the proponents themselves, which is the point of the quote but is not independent confirmation.
Pew and Gallup polls on one state: neither asks the question; only the Pulse, the Peace Index and PCPSR do.

The Israeli right's one-state proposals with citizenship for Palestinians (annexation with equal rights) are not on the card, only annexation without votes; the card has no Fatah or Palestinian Authority statement on one state versus two beyond Abbas's UN speech.
The 2014 Palestinian bureau figures (4.62 million in the West Bank and Gaza) on the INSS/Jerusalem Post page are a different year from the 2025 figures on F1 and do not support them.

The inflation case from its authors' latest publication: the American Research Initiative's own latest study was not found; Ettinger's 2022 JNS opinion piece is the latest we read, and it cites a study 'conducted since 2004' without giving its figures, so the 1.1 million overstatement rests on his 2015 Jerusalem Post statement and the 2005-06 study.

Fatah's own documents or a Fatah leader's statement on one state or two: not found in a page we could read; the Authority's position rests on Abbas's UN address as reported by the UN and CBC. Hamas's text is quoted from the Jewish Virtual Library's copy of the English version; the Arabic original and the 1988 charter were not read.
Coalition agreements and party platforms on annexation: not found; the annexation position comes from Smotrich's and Katz's statements as reported, Ynet's party questionnaire and one Knesset vote.
not_claimed: The numbers do not decide what is just: a population's size does not settle whether its members should have equal rights, a state of their own, or a veto over the other's.

It does not claim that parity exists: the counts range from about 48 percent Jewish to about 60 percent depending on who counts, what is included (Gaza, East Jerusalem, 'others', foreign workers) and what year.
It does not say any party's position is the position of its voters, or that polls predict what any people will accept in practice.
It does not say Smotrich's plan is the Israeli government's policy, or that Said and Beinart speak for Palestinians or for Jews.
Listing who rejects which outcome does not by itself assign blame.

answer_claims.says: One state with equal votes would put Jews and Arabs at or near parity.
Israel counts 7.79 million Jews and 'others' and 2.16 million Arabs; the Palestinian bureau counts 5.56 million in the West Bank and Gaza, East Jerusalem's Arabs in both.
Yoram Ettinger of the American-Israel Demographic Research Group calls the Palestinian count inflated; DellaPergola and Soffer reject that.
In DellaPergola's long-run 2024 projection, adding the West Bank to Israel leaves Jews about 60 percent, and adding Gaza just above 50.
Israeli parties such as Yashar! oppose moves that would endanger the Jewish majority; one-state advocates such as Said and Beinart ask for equal votes.

Our reading: one state with equal votes risks a Jewish majority, annexation without votes denies equal rights, and two states on the 1967 lines would keep both at the price of a border; the numbers explain the choice, they do not make it.

skeptic.notes: ROUND 2 (after the writer's rework). Rechecked new facts; all quotes found online. PCBS (F1): the Palestinian bureau's own 31 December 2025 release says 5.56 million, 3.43 million West Bank, Gaza 2.13 million after a 10.6 percent fall; fixed my earlier must-fix. But every Palestinian figure is one dataset and the text now says so; OCHA's 2.1 million page names no source (reworded 'presumably'). F0: CBS release, Ynet quoting it and DellaPergola's CBS-based projection are one dataset; added to the text. F2: Michael's hedged 2015 line, a UN page that does not mention the overlap, and DellaPergola's 2005 statement that his estimates do not double count East Jerusalem (the card now carries that counter-fact); still one source for the claim. F3: Ettinger's 4 May 2022 JNS opinion piece (opinion, former ambassador) is now carried with its claims (500,000 overseas residents, 370,000 emigrants), so the latest 'inflated' case is present though not its newest study. Hamas 2017 (F10): article 20 'formula of national consensus' with 'no recognition of the legitimacy of the Zionist entity' (article 19) is on the JVL English text; quoted faithfully. Abbas at the UN on 25 September 2025: UN press release and CBC. Smotrich (F6): 3 September 2025 Reuters words and JNS words exact, no motive added; Passal's quote had no date or occasion, fixed in the text (page undated); the Knesset 25 to 24 vote of 22 October 2025 is Al Jazeera ('and news agencies', agency unnamed, one source); Katz and Likud ministers are attributed to the Yesha Council via Israel National News. Wire: Ynet/AP and Global/Reuters marked; CBC checked, not agency copy. Still missing: Fatah documents, coalition agreements, party platforms, the latest 'inflated' study (writer says so). Blocking facts: F0 (one dataset: needs a non-CBS check or accept it as CBS-only and say so), F1 (one dataset, PCBS; the UN Population Division is the independent check), F2 (two sources), F3 (Azure, JPost; advocacy for the rest; Berkley is a blog), F4 (AP and INSS; Berkley blog), F7 (JPost op-ed, Jewish Currents; My Jewish Learning is advocacy). F0 and F1 could simply be marked as single-dataset facts rather than three-source facts.
